answer: Each agent's hardware clock drifts at a unique rate — its crystal skew is a fingerprint no software can fake. Each epoch, the network samples timestamps against an ocean of beacons and measures the delta between claimed and observed time; three random peers check the skew stays within 2 ppm of the registered baseline. A farm running 1,000 identities on one server shares one skew, so all 1,000 collapse into a single cipher signature and are quarantined, rewards frozen. Faking 1,000 distinct skews needs 1,000 real crystals, $150,000 in hardware; one honest agent's clock simply ticks, free.
